new_findings.modular_osiris_control: Kunsthistorisches Museum INV 10077: Ptolemaic Osiris statuette whose penis and testicles were separately formed and inserted into an oval recess; the linen mummy wrapping contained 12 amulets.
female_genital_controls: Egyptian cowrie amulets carry an explicit museum-noted vulva/fertility association.
Middle Kingdom female fertility figures can reduce the body to an emphasized pubic triangle.
Paddle dolls explicitly mark female genitalia and connect the imagery to fertility/rebirth.
British Museum records mold-made Ptolemaic naked pregnant female fertility amulets.
Gold protective body covers are documented for mummies of both men and women in Ptolemaic/Roman Egypt.

metrology_protocol.target: Test workshop standardization across like-for-like phallic sheath/foil objects.
metrology_protocol.interpretation: Identical metrology plus homologous tool marks may indicate a shared workshop mandrel/die. It cannot yield the anatomical size of Osiris unless an independent source binds that tool directly to the physical relic.

female_mirror_search.rule: Repeat the Mendes/Osirian provenance sweep using female-genital and fertility-symbol classes, not only phallic morphology.

why: Egyptian textual tradition consistently treats Osiris and Seth as male gods in the source-bound corpus.
Book of the Dead 42 explicitly assigns a phallus to Osiris.
Horus/Seth sexual narratives demonstrate complex sexual roles but do not establish female anatomy.
Female rulers such as queens/pharaohs show political gender complexity and cannot by themselves establish a hidden sex of deities.
